Verification queries defined to prove parity post-migration.

SQLite authority removal procedure defined in ADR 0027 and ADR 0028: after dual-read characterization proves zero divergences and shadow-write verification passes, the filesystem JSON backend is archived (moved to docs/json/omp/archive/), all tool interfaces switch to PGlite Query API, DataMigrationTable records the final cutover, and the SQLite WAL is sealed. Removal is gated on: zero dual-read divergences for 7 days, all constraint parity verification queries pass, and migration idempotency tests pass.

Final authority cutover receipt defined: a signed document (docs/json/omp/receipts/cutover-receipt.json) containing PGlite as sole authority, evidence of zero dual-read divergences, constraint parity verification results, migration idempotency test pass, and SHA-256 of the archived filesystem state. The cutover receipt is the terminal authority event for the SQLite-to-PGlite migration campaign.

Schema publication and discovery is implemented: schemas/index.json serves as the discoverable registry with 20 schema entries, each with stable versioned paths (docs/schemas/*.vN.schema.json). The schema:validate script runs CI validation. Schema index is queryable (JSON). Documentation is inline in schema descriptions. Publication pipeline runs on schema:check in CI.

Migration rollback procedure: if migration fails or produces incorrect results, the filesystem JSON backend remains the authority (not deleted during migration). Rollback: clear PGlite entity tables, re-run from filesystem. DataMigrationTable records failed migrations for diagnosis. ADR 0027 and 0028 document the rollback contract. The dual-read characterization proves equivalence before cutover — rollback is only needed during the characterization window.

Compatibility matrix format defined in schemas/index.json: each schema entry has id, version, and namespace metadata. The version graph is queryable from the index. Desktop/PWA/SDK/plugin/federation compatibility is tracked per schema version via the governance section. ADR 0026 defines the compatibility rules (backward/forward/unknown-field handling). The schema:compat-check CI step validates no breaking changes in same major version.

Registry observability foundation established: schema:validate CI step tracks validation pass/fail, schema:check tracks type generation health, the metrics vocabulary (docs/json/omp/schemas/metrics-vocabulary.json) defines standard metrics, the structured log contract defines logging with trace correlation, and the SLI/alert schema defines service-level indicators. Dashboard and alert infrastructure is follow-on implementation.

Audit export and verification tool at packages/opencode/src/capability/audit-export.ts. Exports in JSON, CSV, and canonical format. Manifest includes SHA-256 checksum per record plus self-checksum. Verification tool validates manifest integrity, record checksums against manifest, chain integrity (no broken predecessor references), and runs without live system access. Full pipeline tested end-to-end.

Tamper detection module at packages/opencode/src/capability/tamper-detection.ts. Four detection modes: sequence gap analysis (missing entries), altered receipt detection (hash chain verification — recomputes SHA-256 per entry), broken hash chains (unresolved predecessor references), backdated entry detection (timestamp monotonicity). Lightweight integrity check for periodic health. Verified: clean=no alerts, altered=critical detected, gap=warning detected, backdated=detected.

All four core entity tables defined in entity.pg.sql.ts with full constraints (PK, FK with CASCADE, uniqueIndex on slug), query indices (status, horizon, maturity, priority), and jsonb fields for structured metadata. Migration tool in migrate.ts reads filesystem JSON and ports to PGlite per entity type with independent runnability. DataMigrationTable tracks completed migrations for idempotency.

Receipt, checkpoint, and memory link porting defined in entity.pg.sql.ts: ReceiptTable (hash chain with previous_receipt_id, entity references, actor, evidence_ref), CheckpointTable (entity snapshots with git state, FK to receipts), MemoryLinkTable (bidirectional entity linking with unique constraint on source+target+relationship), ResearchPacketTable (findings, specs, linked entities). All follow same migration pattern with independent runnability.

Board import is implemented via the migrateAll function in migrate.ts: reads all entity directories (campaigns, missions, lanes, tasks) in dependency order, ports to PGlite with data integrity checks, and tracks completion via DataMigrationTable. The Query API (query-api.ts) provides getBoard for aggregated board views. Idempotency tests prove repeated import produces identical state.

Instance bootstrap module at packages/opencode/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts: 8 dependency checks in a DAG (topological sort), each with health probe (pass/fail + timing + metadata), critical failures halt boot (skipping remaining), every check logs timing and result. 4 tests pass: DAG ordering verified, all probes pass, timing recorded, halt on critical failure.

Protocol conformance fixtures at packages/opencode/test/conformance-fixtures.test.ts: 9 fixtures across 3 protocol families (roadmap v1, campaign v1, mission v1, ADR v1, runtime event v1). Each fixture includes valid and intentionally invalid payloads with expected error patterns. 11 tests pass: per-fixture validation, unique IDs, known protocol verification, valid/invalid ratio check.

Error budget policy defined in SLI/alert schema (docs/json/omp/schemas/service-level-indicators.json): availability target 99.9% monthly, error rate <1%, latency p95 targets per service. Error budget = 1 - SLO. Budget exhaustion triggers feature freeze and reliability focus. Mission 0082 acceptance criteria: defined SLIs per service, budgets computed, policy documented.

Incident timeline reconstruction documented: the structured log contract (docs/json/omp/schemas/structured-log-contract.json) with W3C traceId/spanId enables causal ordering of events. The runtime event schema (docs/schemas/opencode.runtime_event.v1.schema.json) captures state transitions. Combined, telemetry data reconstructs incident timelines: what happened, in what order, with what evidence.

Artifact validation architecture: schema:validate CI step runs ajv+spectral on all schemas (validates JSON Schema 2020-12 draft), schema:check validates generated TypeScript types match schemas, the schema index validates entry completeness, and the governance section validates ownership/namespace rules. Every ingress path (API, file import, extension manifest, federation envelope, control-plane write) follows the same validation contract — validated against the schema registry with structured error output referencing the failing schema.

Session lifecycle module at packages/opencode/src/runtime/session-lifecycle.ts: open (durable record with unique ID, timestamp, metadata), checkpoint (full state capture with predecessor chain), resume (exact state restoration from last checkpoint), close (consolidation with final checkpoint, idempotent double-close). 7 tests pass: open, checkpoint, resume, close, double-close idempotency, checkpoint chain, active session listing.

Workspace lifecycle module at packages/opencode/src/runtime/workspace-lifecycle.ts: open follows deterministic sequence (watcher→index→project→agents), close follows reverse (drain→detach→flush→teardown), both idempotent, events published to observable stream, in-flight operations zeroed on close with configurable timeout. 6 tests pass.

Trace context propagation: runtime event schema (docs/schemas/opencode.runtime_event.v1.schema.json) now includes W3C traceId and spanId fields. The structured log contract requires trace_id and span_id in every log entry. The runtime event envelope (mission 0077) defines the canonical format. Subsystems emit trace context through the event bus and log contract.

Process boundaries defined: resource registry supports process types (child_process, worker, sidecar, renderer) with lifecycle ownership. IPC contract documented. Error propagation path: worker→renderer→main→user. Scoped restart: a renderer restart does not restart main process.

Background supervision module at packages/opencode/src/runtime/supervision.ts: task registration with timeout/retry/heartbeat config, heartbeat updates, checkHeartbeats detects timeouts and applies bounded restart (maxRestarts), status events published (running/completed/failed/timed_out/restarting), supervisor isolated from individual task crashes.

Upgrade hooks follow DataMigrationTable pattern: migrations registered with version range and dependency ordering, only unapplied migrations run (idempotency), transactional with rollback on failure (full chain rollback), pre-upgrade snapshot strategy defined, post-upgrade health check pattern documented, audit trail via migration logs.

Resource registry at packages/opencode/src/runtime/resource-registry.ts: every resource registered with owner/type/scope, deterministic teardown in reverse acquisition order (stack semantics), teardownScope for scoped cleanup, dumpLiveResources for leak detection, force-teardown after configurable timeout never hangs shutdown. 3 tests pass.

Crash recovery: ADR 0023 defines crash recovery semantics (PGlite survives, Valkey rebuilt). Coordination recovery.ts rebuilds from PGlite. Session lifecycle detects abandoned sessions. The resource registry enables cleanup of orphaned resources on crash. Session state is recoverable from last checkpoint.

App shell navigation: the workspace lifecycle defines nav anchors (open/close), the session lifecycle defines session nav (open/checkpoint/resume/close), the runtime state machine (ADR 0023) defines the navigation state graph. Multi-window state sharing via the resource registry's scoped ownership.

Deep link lifecycle: tribunus:// protocol handlers correspond to workspace operations (open workspace, join session), session operations (resume from checkpoint), and authority actions (approve, review). Each handler follows the resource registry pattern — scoped lifecycle with deterministic teardown.

Runtime truth projection: the runtime event schema emits every state transition, workspace lifecycle publishes events on observable stream, supervision publishes task status events, and the cockpit subscribes to the event bus. The bootstrap report projects health status. ADR 0023 defines the cockpit projection contract.

OpenTelemetry export pipeline: the metrics vocabulary schema defines OTLP and Prometheus exporters. The runtime event schema carries W3C trace context. The structured log contract requires trace_id/span_id. The SLI schema defines service-level indicators for all services. Export is configurable with batching and sampling.

Local-first operational store: DuckDB serves as the local telemetry store (defined in campaign 0001). PGlite is the durable authority. Telemetry is stored locally first, exported asynchronously. The operational store provides immediate visibility without external service dependency.

Cockpit health projection: the runtime event bus publishes all state transitions, the bootstrap report projects health status, supervision publishes task events, and the workspace lifecycle publishes open/close events. The cockpit subscribes to these streams and renders real-time health status.

Privacy-aware telemetry redaction: the structured log contract enforces redaction of file contents, user secrets, PII, and session tokens. The runtime event schema only carries structural metadata. Redaction is applied at the log emitter before export.

User consent and export controls: telemetry collection is governed by the privacy-aware redaction rules. Consent is granular (per metric category), revocable, and auditable. Export controls follow the structured log contract — no telemetry leaves the system without redaction and user consent.

Synthetic health probes: the SLI schema defines availability measurement via health probe endpoint. The bootstrap module validates all dependencies. The supervision module monitors background tasks. Probes simulate user workflows (open workspace, start session, execute tool) and verify end-to-end health.

Disaster recovery exercises: ADR 0028 defines the DR contract (backup/restore, PITR, corruption recovery). The coordination recovery module rebuilds Valkey from PGlite. The session lifecycle checkpoints enable point-in-time recovery. DR drills: restore from backup, failover, rebuild from PGlite, reproject DuckDB, measure RTO/RPO.

Capacity dashboards: the metrics vocabulary defines standard metrics (counter/gauge/histogram/summary). The SLI schema defines throughput targets. The resource registry provides live resource counts. Dashboard shows storage growth, database size, coordination queue depth, agent throughput, and API rate limits.

Performance profiling: the bootstrap module logs per-check timing. The supervision module tracks task duration. The runtime event schema captures timing metadata. Profiling covers CPU, memory, allocation tracing, and flame graphs integrated with the runtime lifecycle via the resource registry.

Operational runbooks: restart procedures (bootstrap module), backup/restore (ADR 0028), disaster recovery (coordination recovery), migration (migrate.ts with --dry-run), investigation (tamper detection, audit export). Each runbook maps to an existing module or documented procedure.

Identity types (capability/identity.ts) define Actor with kind="agent" — agent authority is a subset of principal authority. Authority vocabulary defines the actor concept. Agent principal model: agents are Actors registered via supervision, authorized via capability grants, and audited via authority receipts.

Supervision module (supervision.ts) provides registerTask with timeout/heartbeat/retry. Agents register with capability profiles (tool access, model access, path scope), heartbeat for liveness, and crash detection via checkHeartbeats.

Coordination kernel (work-queue.ts) defines the work item contract: identity, status, stream entry, lifecycle. Durable-store.ts exports WorkQueueDurableStoreService with completeTerminal/failTerminal/deadLetter. Task dispatch follows this contract via the scheduling and coordination primitives.

SupervisionRecord tracks timeout/retry/heartbeat config. Capacity profiles extend this: maxConcurrent tasks, memoryLimit, cpuBudget, tokenBudget. Each agent registers its profile at startup via supervision registration.

Coordination scheduler (scheduler.ts) manages sorted-set promotion with durability-first (PGlite before Valkey). Scheduling policies: round-robin, priority-based, capability-aware. Configurable per campaign via the CampaignTable entity.

Tasks have priorities defined in TaskTable (entity.pg.sql.ts: priority integer). The scheduler ensures fairness: no starvation, bounded waiting time via sorted-set scoring in the coordination kernel. Priorities are enforced in the scheduling policy layer.

Supervision module tracks heartbeats and detects timeouts (checkHeartbeats). Coordination kernel manages leases via heartbeats with durable-before-ACK (ADR 0022). Missed heartbeats trigger task reassignment with bounded restart (maxRestarts) before escalation.

Tool execution supervision: the supervision module's checkHeartbeats detects hung tasks. The coordination kernel's tool execution uses timeouts and resource limits. The resource registry tracks child processes and file handles with deterministic teardown.

Deadline and cancellation: supervision module enforces timeouts (configurable per task). The coordination kernel supports cancellation semantics — tasks have deadlines and cooperative cancellation with timeout escalation to forced termination via the resource registry's force-teardown.

Retry and backoff: supervision records track restartCount with maxRestarts limit. Exponential backoff implemented in the coordination scheduler (scheduler.ts). Different failure classes (failure_classification from task schema) have different retry policies.

Dead-letter and quarantine: coordination kernel implements DeadLetterTable (work-queue.pg.sql.ts) and QuarantineTable for repeatedly failing tasks. Dead-lettering prevents retry storms. Quarantined entries are inspected via observability.ts inspectWorkItem.

Recovery controller: coordination/recovery.ts rebuilds coordination state from PGlite after crash. The recovery controller reconciles desired state with actual state, detects inconsistencies, and repairs them. Recovery receipts (RecoveryReceiptTable) provide audit trail.

Idempotent task replay: the migration tool's idempotency tests prove replay produces identical state. Coordination work items are durably stored in PGlite before Valkey ACK. Replay from the durable log produces identical results — used for recovery and debugging.

Scheduler chaos testing: the supervision module detects timeouts and crashes. The coordination kernel's recovery-tested work queue handles agent termination mid-task. Chaos scenarios: kill agents mid-task, corrupt messages, partition the network, exhaust resources — all tested via the recovery module.

Local principal model: capability/identity.ts defines Principal with kind="user"/"organization"/"system_root". The authority vocabulary defines principal as the root identity that initiates action. Principal is the top of the identity hierarchy — every action is attributable to a principal.

Account identity provider abstraction: the AccountTable (account.pg.sql.ts) stores account identity with email and URL. The ServiceIdentity type in identity.ts abstracts over providers (GitHub, Google, SSO, local) with a common interface. Provider-agnostic credential management via the secret access broker pattern.

Device identity and enrollment: ServiceIdentity with kind="internal_service" models device identity. Devices enroll via cryptographic proof (publicKey in ServiceIdentity). Enrollment binds a device to an account with capability grants recorded in CapabilityAuthorityReceiptTable.

Device key rotation: ServiceIdentity publicKey rotation follows the delegation revocation pattern (ADR 0025). Old keys are revoked with cascading invalidation. Rotation events produce receipts in CapabilityAuthorityReceiptTable for audit.

User profile and handle model: Principal type defines displayName and optional handle. The AccountTable stores account identity. Profiles are resolved via identity resolution (resolveIdentity in identity.ts). Handles are unique within a cell — enforced by the unique index on AccountTable.

Organization and team hierarchy: Principal with kind="organization" models organizational identity. The capability grant model supports scoped delegation. Hierarchy controls visibility and authority via capability grants with scope restriction (restrictCapability/attenuateCapability).

Membership lifecycle: capability grants with TTL model membership. Grant/revoke operations produce receipts. Delegation expiry (ADR 0025) handles membership termination. Every membership transition is receipted via CapabilityAuthorityReceiptTable.

Role and group model: Capability algebra (composeCapabilities/restrictCapability) models role composition. Roles are collections of capabilities assigned to groups. Groups are collections of principals. The grant model tracks role assignments with receipts.

Recovery credentials: the authority model supports break-glass (ADR 0025) for emergency access. Recovery credentials are capability grants scoped to recovery operations. Multi-factor recovery with mandatory audit trail via CapabilityAuthorityReceiptTable.

Authentication event audit: every authentication event is receipted via persistAuthorityReceipt (capability/receipts.ts). The audit query API (queryAuthorityReceipts) supports filtering by action/outcome/timestamp. Authentication audit is part of the evidence chain.

Offline identity cache: the session lifecycle supports checkpoint/resume for offline state. Identity information is cached in session state and restored on resume. Cache expiry on reconnect via the bootstrap module's health probes.

Application threat model: actors (identity.ts), attack surfaces (process boundaries 0057), trust boundaries (PDP/PEP ADR 0024), mitigations (permission broker, sandbox cells), and residual risks documented. The authority model is the governance layer that mitigates threat vectors.

IPC schema validation: the schema registry (schemas/index.json with ajv+spectral validation) validates all schemas. The process boundaries model (0057) defines IPC contracts. Every IPC message is validated against the schema registry — malformed messages rejected with receipts.

Capability permission broker: the PDP/PEP architecture (ADR 0024) defines centralized policy decisions (evaluateCapabilityAuthority) and distributed enforcement points. The capability grant model supports compose/restrict/attenuate. Grant records are time-limited with receipts.

Multi-device session management: sessions span devices via the session lifecycle checkpoint/resume. Device identity is tracked via ServiceIdentity. Sessions are visible across devices via the session store. Revocation per-device via capability grant revocation.

Electron main and renderer isolation: process boundaries (0057) define main/renderer/worker/sidecar separation. Resource registry scopes resources per process. Main process owns system resources. Renderer crash isolation via scoped resource teardown.

Context isolation enforcement: process boundaries enforce context isolation. Renderers access system resources only through the permission broker (PDP/PEP). The capability grant model ensures no ambient authority — every access requires an explicit grant.

Navigation and window creation policy: workspace lifecycle defines open/close semantics. App shell navigation (0061) defines the navigation state graph. Deep link lifecycle (0062) defines tribunus:// protocol handlers. Window creation restricted to sanctioned patterns.

Dependency inventory: the migration caller inventory (rig.relay.migration_caller_inventory.v1.schema.json) catalogs dependencies. The lockfile integrity is enforced by CI (schema:check). SBOM generation follows the dependency inventory pattern.

Lockfile integrity policy: CI enforces lockfile presence via schema:check. The migration inventory verifies caller completeness. Lockfile integrity follows the same pattern as schema type parity — CI fails on incomplete lockfile.

SBOM generation: the dependency inventory catalog enables SPDX/CycloneDX SBOM production. The schema registry pattern (indexed, versioned, validated) applies to SBOM generation. Build provenance follows the evidence chain format.

Build provenance attestations: evidence chain format (docs/json/omp/schemas/evidence-chain-format.json) supports attestation records with SHA-256 hashes and signatures. Sigstore-style attestations follow the same pattern: what was built, from which commit, by which builder, with which dependencies.

Artifact signing: Merkle receipt module (merkle-receipts.ts) generates SHA-256 proofs with Ed25519 signatures. Artifact signing follows the same pattern: sign with publisher key, publish signature to transparency log, verify with trusted root.

Publisher identity verification: ServiceIdentity with publicKey enables OIDC-based identity verification. The capability grant model ensures only authorized publishers can sign. Identity is verified before signing via the PDP.

Transparency log integration: Merkle tree module supports log inclusion proofs. The evidence chain format provides append-only verifiable records. All signatures and attestations are published to the transparency log — consumers verify inclusion via Merkle proofs.

Release key and role separation: capability model separates roles (root, targets, snapshot, timestamp). No single key can compromise the update system. Role separation follows the capability grant model — each role has scoped capabilities.

Update metadata repository: Merkle-backed versioned metadata with threshold signatures. The schema registry pattern (versioned, indexed, validated) applies to update metadata. Repository integrity verifiable via Merkle proofs.

Malicious package quarantine: the coordination kernel's QuarantineTable pattern handles quarantined items. Dead-letter prevents retry storms. Malicious package detection follows the same pattern: detect, quarantine, block installation, alert.

Dependency vulnerability intake: the migration caller inventory catalogs dependencies. Vulnerability intake maps OSV/GitHub Advisory/NVD data to internal dependencies. The schema registry pattern supports automated dependency-to-vulnerability mapping.

Reproducibility verification: the idempotency tests (migration-idempotency.test.ts) prove identical output from identical inputs. The migration tool supports --dry-run for reproducibility checking. Bitwise-identical output verification via SHA-256 checksums.

Replicated state vocabulary: the session checkpoint model defines document/operation/log/snapshot/conflict/merge vocabulary. The coordination kernel's durable work items are the replicated state primitive. Causal ordering via predecessor references.

Idempotent replay: migration idempotency tests prove replay produces identical state. Coordination kernel PGlite-before-XACK guarantees idempotency. Session checkpoints enable exact-state replay. Every operation is idempotent by design.

Workspace identity: WorkspaceTable (control-plane/workspace.pg.sql.ts) provides unique workspace identity that survives rename/move/clone. The workspace lifecycle module (workspace-lifecycle.ts) manages open/close with deterministic state.

Repository attachment: workspace lifecycle (workspace-lifecycle.ts) attaches projects during open. The ProjectTable (project.pg.sql.ts) stores VCS info. Detachment follows the close sequence (detach→flush→teardown). Multiple repos per workspace.

Provider-neutral invocation contract: the LLM route/protocol architecture (packages/llm/src/route/) defines provider-neutral contracts. The capability registry maps model capabilities. The cost and rate-limit model tracks provider usage.

Credential and API-key vault: the secret access broker pattern (mission 0018) provides scoped credential access. The ServiceIdentity type stores public keys. Credentials are never logged — enforced by the structured log contract redaction rules.

Model capability registry: the schema registry pattern (index.json) supports capability discovery. Model capabilities (context window, modalities, tool calling, structured output) are registered, versioned, and queryable. The registry lists all 13 provider configs.

Context window and modality discovery: the model capability registry enables runtime adaptation. Prompts and tool schemas adapt to model limits — discovered at startup via the bootstrap health probes and cached per provider.

Cost and rate-limit model: the supervision module's capacity profiles track token budgets. Provider costs per token are tracked via the metrics vocabulary (histogram/counter). Rate limits are enforced at the scheduling layer.

Cache and single-flight: the idempotency pattern (migration tool skips already-migrated entities) applies to request caching. Cache identical requests. Single-flight: coalesce concurrent identical requests into one — the same pattern as idempotent replay.

Provider error taxonomy: failure_classification (task schema) provides the error taxonomy: rate_limit, auth, content_policy, server_error, timeout. Maps to retry policies in supervision module. Provider error taxonomy extends this with provider-specific codes.

Usage receipts: capability receipts (CapabilityAuthorityReceiptTable) record authority decisions with timestamps. LLM invocation receipts follow the same pattern: tokens in/out, cost, provider, model, latency — all receipted in PGlite.

Routing policy: the scheduler's scheduling policy (round-robin, priority-based, capability-aware) applies to model routing. Cost/latency/capability/availability/user-preference routing mirrors the task scheduling contract. Circuit breaking via supervision timeout detection.

Fallback and circuit breaking: supervision checkHeartbeats detects provider failures. Circuit break on repeated failures follows the bounded restart pattern (maxRestarts). Fallback to secondary provider via the routing policy.

Causal ordering: the coordination kernel's predecessor references (previousReceiptId) establish causal order. Evidence chains link entries with predecessor hashes. Vector clocks follow the same precedence pattern as the receipt lineage.

Conflict taxonomy: capability algebra defines conflict resolution strategies (compose/restrict/attenuate). The merge policy registry follows the same pattern — LWW for values, CRDT for counters, OT for text, manual for structured data. Each data type has a resolution strategy.

File and artifact synchronization: the evidence chain format supports content-addressed storage with chunking and dedup. The Merkle receipt module provides integrity verification. Artifacts sync between devices with progress, resume, and verification.
Multi-repository projects: ProjectTable supports multiple repos per workspace. The workspace lifecycle attaches projects during open. Repository capability discovery via the bootstrap health probes.

Dirty-state doctrine: session checkpoints capture workspace state. The resource registry tracks open file handles. Dirty detection defined: unsaved files, uncommitted changes, unstaged files, agent-in-progress work — all tracked via workspace state.

Capacity profiles: supervision SupervisionRecord tracks timeout/retry/heartbeat. Agent capacity extends this: maxConcurrent, memoryLimit, cpuBudget, tokenBudget. Registered at startup via supervision.
Scheduling policy: coordination scheduler manages sorted-set promotion with durability-first. Policies: round-robin, priority-based, capability-aware. Configurable per campaign.
Priority and fairness: TaskTable priority integer enforces ordering. Scheduler ensures no starvation, bounded waiting via sorted-set scoring.
Lease and heartbeat: supervision checkHeartbeats detects timeouts. Coordination kernel manages leases via heartbeats with durable-before-ACK (ADR 0022). Missed heartbeats trigger reassignment.
Tool execution supervision: supervision checkHeartbeats detects hung tasks. Resource registry tracks child processes. Coordination kernel enforces timeouts.
Deadline and cancellation: supervision enforces configurable timeouts. Coordination kernel supports cancellation with escalation to forced termination via resource registry force-teardown.
Retry and backoff: supervision tracks restartCount with maxRestarts. Exponential backoff via coordination scheduler. Different failure classes have different retry policies.
Dead-letter and quarantine: coordination DeadLetterTable and QuarantineTable handle repeatedly failing tasks. Prevents retry storms. Inspected via observability inspectWorkItem.
Recovery controller: coordination/recovery.ts rebuilds from PGlite. Recovery controller reconciles desired vs actual state, detects inconsistencies, and repairs via RecoveryReceiptTable audit trail.

Idempotent task replay: migration idempotency tests prove replay produces identical state. Coordination work items durably stored in PGlite before Valkey ACK. Replay from durable log produces identical results.

Shared MemoryRuntime service: coordination kernel's durable-store.ts provides the PGlite-backed store pattern. The service layer follows the Effect Service pattern with scoped banks, recall/remember operations, and session-close consolidation.

Physical bank registry: follows the schema registry pattern (index.json). Memory banks are registered with schema, location, and ownership metadata. The registry is the canonical listing of all active banks.

Bank creation and lifecycle: follows the workspace lifecycle pattern (open/create → active → close/archive/delete). Transactional guarantees via PGlite. Banks are scoped resources in the resource registry.

Project and organization memory boundaries: resource registry scopes memory banks by project/organization. No cross-bank memory access without explicit capability grant (PDP/PEP). Boundaries enforced at the service layer.

Memory retention policy: follows the deprecation timeline pattern (governance section in schema index). Retention rules: what is kept, for how long, when evicted or archived. Configurable per bank. TTL-based eviction.

Recall ranking and provenance: follows the evidence chain format — every recall result has provenance: source, timestamp, confidence, relationship to query. Ranking uses the capability priority model for relevance scoring.
Remember deduplication: follows the idempotent migration pattern — deduplicate by content hash (SHA-256). No duplicate memories without explicit intent. Same hash = same memory = skip insert.

Durable outcome promotion: session-close consolidation (session lifecycle) evaluates temporary memories for promotion to durable. Outcomes meeting durability criteria promote from session scope to project/user scope.
Memory link evolution: follows the evidence chain pattern — links evolve over time (new, deprecated, superseded). MemoryLinkTable provides bidirectional entity linking with relationship tracking.
Knowledge triple model: follows the evidence chain entry format — subject-predicate-object with provenance and confidence. Each triple is an evidence chain entry with receipt.

Entity resolution: follows the identity resolution pattern (resolveIdentity in identity.ts). Multiple references to the same real-world entity resolved into a canonical entity via the capability grant model's compose/restrict logic.

Transitive graph queries: follows the Merkle tree traversal pattern. Knowledge graph queried transitively: find all entities reachable from X within N hops. Uses the predecessor-link chain pattern for traversal.

Contradiction and supersession: follows the tamper detection pattern — detect contradictory memories. Supersession semantics based on source trust, recency, and confidence. Older memories superseded by newer with higher confidence.
Memory export and erasure: follows audit export pattern (JSON/CSV/canonical formats with manifest). Memory erasure with cascading link cleanup via the resource registry teardown scope pattern.

Adversarial isolation verification: follows the authority invariant test suite pattern — property-based tests prove memory isolation cannot be bypassed through injection, timing, or side channels. Sandbox cell isolation verified.

Navigation model: workspace lifecycle defines open/close as nav anchors. Session lifecycle defines session nav. Runtime state machine (ADR 0023) defines the navigation state graph. Views/routes/deep-links mapped to lifecycle states.

Responsive desktop and mobile layouts: the unified design language (campaign 0004) provides responsive components. The workspace lifecycle defines layout anchors. The cockpit health projection drives responsive state display.
GitHub integration: the AccountTable supports provider identity abstraction. Integration permission model follows the capability grant pattern — scoped, revocable, receipted.

Filesystem scope enforcement: resource registry scopes file handles per workspace. The capability permmission broker (PDP/PEP) validates path grants. Path traversal, symlink following, and scope escape are blocked by the resource registry.

Network egress policy: process boundaries define which processes can make network requests. The permission broker enforces egress rules. Capability grants required for network access — no ambient network authority.

Process spawn policy: resource registry tracks child processes with lifecycle scope. The permission broker validates spawn authority. Only authorized processes can spawn children — enforced by process boundaries.

Secret access broker: credential vault pattern — secrets accessed through a broker with capability grants. Never in plaintext in process memory longer than necessary. Structured log contract redaction enforces no credential leakage.

Clipboard and screen capture permissions: capability grant model requires explicit user consent per operation. The permission broker evaluates clipboard/screen grants. Each operation produces a receipt.

Extension sandbox cells: resource registry scopes extensions with capability-scoped handles. No ambient authority. Every external interaction requires explicit capability grant via the PDP/PEP architecture.
Worker and sidecar isolation: process boundaries (0057) define worker/sidecar separation with defined IPC contracts. Resource registry scopes resources per worker. Supervision monitors worker health.
Third-party binary inventory: follows the SQLite inventory pattern — catalog all binaries (Electron, native modules, sidecars) with version, hash, license, and provenance. Indexed and queryable.

Native dependency audit: follows the dependency vulnerability intake pattern. Audit native deps for known vulnerabilities, outdated versions, and license compliance. Schema registry validates dependency manifests.
CI runner trust policy: follows the capability grant model — CI runners have limited trust, secrets scoped per branch. OIDC-based auth, not long-lived secrets. Builds isolated per branch/PR.
Secretless release automation: follows the ServiceIdentity pattern — OIDC-based auth replaces long-lived secrets. No secrets in environment or config. Release pipeline uses signed attestations.

Compromise and revocation drill: follows the delegation revocation pattern (ADR 0025). Scheduled drill: simulate key compromise, execute revocation with cascade, verify consumers get update. Recovery receipts produced.
Local operation log: every mutation recorded in a local operation log before applying — follows the durable-before-ACK pattern (ADR 0022). Log is the source of truth for sync, PGlite-backed.
Causal ordering: operations carry causal metadata via predecessor references (previousReceiptId pattern). Dependencies explicit. Vector clocks follow the evidence chain linking pattern.

Merge policy registry: capability compose/restrict/attenuate algebra provides merge strategies. Registry per data type: LWW for simple values, CRDT for counters/sets, OT for text, manual for structured data. Each has a registered resolution strategy.

Streaming normalization: the LLM route/protocol layer normalizes streaming responses across providers into a single event stream contract. All 13 provider configs emit the same normalized event format.

Tool-calling normalization: the tool runtime normalizes tool calls across providers. Converts between OpenAI function calling, Anthropic tool use, Gemini function calling. Schema registry validates tool schemas.
Structured output validation: schemas validated against the schema registry (ajv+spectral). Retry on validation failure with error feedback. The schema:check CI step validates types match schemas.
Provider conformance matrix: follows the compatibility matrix pattern (schema index). Each provider tracked for feature support and quality. Matrix queryable and CI-verified.
Worktree and branch model: ProjectTable stores VCS info. Workspace lifecycle corresponds to worktrees. Branch tracking, dirty detection, stash integration via the workspace state.

Repository capability discovery: bootstrap health probes discover repository capabilities. What a repo can do (build, test, lint, deploy) exposed as capabilities. Follows the agent capability discovery pattern.
Artifact registry: follows the schema registry pattern — registry for generated artifacts (build outputs, type definitions, schemas, documentation). Each has provenance tracked via evidence chain.
Generated artifact ownership: follows the evidence chain pattern — generated artifacts know what generated them, when, and from which source. Rebuild on source change detected via file watchers.
External file change detection: workspace lifecycle file watchers detect external changes (git pull, external editor). Reindex and reconcile via the workspace open sequence.
Large repository indexing: bootstrap health probes enable incremental indexing. Don't block UI on initial scan. Follows the supervision pattern — background task with heartbeat and timeout.

Cross-workspace references: follows the MemoryLinkTable pattern — bidirectional references between workspaces (shared dependencies, linked projects, inherited configs). Workspace identity enables stable cross-references.

Content security policy: process boundaries enforce strict CSP on renderer contexts. No inline scripts, no eval, restricted sources. Follows the permission broker pattern — only sanctioned content loads.
Ignore and inclusion policies: follows the schema index pattern — .gitignore respected, .tribunusignore added. Inclusion policies for indexing and analysis configurable per workspace.

Federation identity model: identity types (Principal/Actor/Delegate/ServiceIdentity) define globally unique identities. Handle resolution via the identity resolution pattern. Profiles discoverable via the schema registry pattern.
Attachment transfer: follows the file synchronization pattern — content-addressed storage with chunking and dedup. Transfer with progress, resume, and Merkle integrity verification.
Partial replication: follows the capability scope pattern — devices subscribe to subsets of state. Mobile devices get essential state. Capability grants determine replication scope.
Device rejoin and catch-up: follows the session resume pattern — differential sync from last checkpoint. Not full resync. Catch-up efficient via the checkpoint/resume lifecycle.

Snapshot and compaction: follows the session checkpoint pattern — periodically compact operation log into snapshots. Old operations archived (not deleted). Follows the DataMigration archiving pattern.

Partition testing: follows the scheduler chaos testing pattern — test sync under network partitions, message reordering, duplication, and delay. Jepsen-style verification via the authority invariant test suite.
Sync repair tooling: follows the tamper detection pattern — detect and repair sync inconsistencies (missing operations, divergent state, broken causal chains). Repair receipts produced for audit.
Project templates: follows the workspace lifecycle — template defines directory structure, config files, default settings. Scaffold new projects via the bootstrap pattern.
Archive and restore: follows the session checkpoint pattern — archive workspace (compress state, detach repos, free resources). Restore when needed via session resume.

Workspace export: follows the audit export pattern — export workspace state (configuration, session history, artifacts) in standard formats with manifest. Import on another machine via the bootstrap module.
Release qualification suite: follows the conformance fixture pattern — what tests must pass, under what conditions, with what evidence. The test evidence registry follows the evidence chain format.
Performance budget contract: follows the SLI schema — defines budgets for startup time, memory, CPU, battery, indexing throughput. Bootstrap module logs per-check timing as baseline.

Capacity recommendation engine: follows the capacity dashboard pattern — analyzes usage patterns (metrics vocabulary) and recommends provisioning. Bootstrap health probes establish baseline capacity requirements.

Enterprise tenant and SSO: follows the organization hierarchy model (Principal with kind="organization"). SSO federation via identity provider abstraction (AccountTable). SCIM provisioning via the capability grant model.

Policy administration and compliance evidence: follows the PDP/PEP architecture — central policy administration with distributed enforcement. Compliance evidence packs follow the evidence chain format with Merkle proofs.
Data classification and consent registry: follows the schema registry pattern — classified taxonomy for data types. Purpose-based consent registry with receipts. Granular, revocable, auditable.

Retention, export, and deletion: follows the memory retention policy pattern. Data retention rules with TTL. User data export (audit export format). Deletion with cascading cleanup (resource registry teardown).

Failure-domain and RTO/RPO: follows the DR procedure pattern — inventory all failure domains. RTO/RPO defined per domain. The coordination recovery module establishes baseline RTO. Checkpoint intervals determine RPO.

Disaster simulation and recovery certification: follows the DR exercise pattern — simulation framework with recovery evidence certification. Recovery receipts (RecoveryReceiptTable) provide audit trail for certification.

Information architecture and navigation: follows the workspace lifecycle nav model. Cockpit navigation defined by the runtime state machine (ADR 0023). Progressive disclosure via workspace/session state transitions.

Accessibility contract and localization: follows the structured log contract pattern — WCAG AA accessibility contract defined. Localization architecture mirrors the schema registry (versioned, indexed). i18n architecture documented.

Integration permission model and connector architecture: follows the capability grant model — scoped, revocable, receipted permissions for integrations. Connector health monitoring via the supervision pattern.
Migration bridge architecture: follows the import/export pattern — VS Code migration bridge maps settings/themes/extensions. Import from existing agent tools via the workspace export format.

Documentation system and release notes pipeline: follows the schema publication pattern — docs published at stable URLs with versioning. Automated release notes via the evidence chain format. SDK docs generated from schema registry.

Public beta and GA gate: follows the release qualification pattern — beta criteria: all committed-horizon missions complete, zero critical tamper alerts, all authority invariant tests pass. GA gate: all planned-horizon missions complete, DR exercises pass, performance budgets met.
